declared.title: Scaling up behavioral science interventions in online education
declared.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « scaling up behavioral science interventions in online education » (2026-11-23)

population: about 250,000 students from nearly every country in 247 online courses (Harvard, MIT, Stanford) over 2.5 years; preregistered waves

findings.text: Self-regulation interventions (plan-making, MCII) raised engagement in the first weeks but not course completion

support.sentence: Self-regulation interventions raised student engagement in the first few weeks but not final completion rates.

findings.text: At scale, MCII did not improve course completion even for students in individualist countries, where it had worked before

support.sentence: The MCII intervention did not improve course completion for students in individualistic countries (year 2: β = 0.25 pp, 95% CI = [−0.87, 1.37], t = 0.44, P = 0.662), and the social accountability intervention did not improve completion rates for students in nonindividualistic countries (year 2: β = 0.89 pp, 95% CI = [−0.22, 1.99], t = 1.58, P = 0.115).

limits: online courses with low completion rates; a light intervention embedded in a survey
results by groups of countries (individualism, development), none for the Arab world
the MCII test is the authors' own replication of their earlier result (kizilcec-2017-culture)
